editorial:
Imagine a classic 80s romance where love is complicated by family drama and emotional clashes. You get to see a young Venkatesh bringing his usual charm to the screen, playing a lead who is caught between his heart and his duties. Along with Farah and Poornima Bhagyaraj, the movie creates a vibe that feels like a warm throwback to an era where songs and long dialogues drove the story. It is a slow-burn drama that focuses more on feelings and relationships than flashy action, making it feel like a cozy movie you would watch on a rainy afternoon.

What really works here is the chemistry between the leads and the way the emotional beats land. While the pacing might feel a bit slow for people used to today's fast movies, the strong acting makes up for it. You might find some of the plot points a bit predictable, but that is part of the charm of these old-school romances. If you can find a restored version to stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, the colors will really pop. Otherwise, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great way to keep this piece of cinema history forever.
endingExplained: The story wraps up after a lot of emotional tension and misunderstandings between the main couple. In the final scenes, the characters finally face their family conflicts and admit their true feelings for one another. After several hurdles and tears, the lovers overcome the obstacles put in their way by their elders. The movie ends on a happy note with the couple uniting, proving that true love wins over social pressure and family pride.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic Telugu cinema and old school love stories.
